text: In his Essay Concerning Human Understanding, Locke locates personal identity over time in:
choices: the persistence of the same immaterial soul or substance
the continuity of consciousness, and in particular memory -- being able to remember one's earlier experiences
the continuous life of the same human organism
the narrative one constructs to make one's life cohere
explanation: Locke deliberately separated the identity of the person (continuity of consciousness/memory) from the identity of substance (the soul), so that identity could persist without a persisting soul. Option 0 is the substance view Locke rejected; option 2 is animalism; option 3 is the later narrative account (Schechtman).
